verses.text: As God's co-workers, we urge you not to receive his grace and then let it go to waste.
For God says, ‘At the right time I heard you; on the day of salvation I helped you.’ Look, now is the right time; now is the day of salvation.
We don't put any obstacle in anyone's way, so our ministry won't be discredited.
Instead, in every way we show that we're God's servants: through great endurance, troubles, hardships, and distress;
through beatings, imprisonments, riots, hard work, sleepless nights, and hunger;
through purity, knowledge, patience, kindness, the Holy Spirit, and sincere love;
through the true message, God's power, and the weapons of righteousness in both hands;
through honor and dishonor, bad reports and good reports; treated as impostors, yet telling the truth;
treated as unknown, yet well known; treated as dying, yet look—we live; punished, but not killed;
grieving, yet always joyful; poor, yet making many rich; having nothing, yet possessing everything.
We've spoken openly to you, Corinthians; our hearts are wide open.
We haven't held back our affection for you, but you've held back yours for us.
So, as my children, open your hearts to us too.
Don't bind yourselves together with unbelievers in a way that compromises your faith. What partnership is there between righteousness and lawlessness? What fellowship does light have with darkness?
What harmony is there between Christ and the devil? What does a believer share with an unbeliever?
What agreement can God's temple have with idols? We are the temple of the living God. As God said, ‘I will live with them and walk among them. I will be their God, and they will be my people.’
So the Lord says, ‘Come out from among them and be separate. Don't touch anything unclean, and I will welcome you.’
‘I will be a Father to you, and you will be my sons and daughters,’ says the Lord Almighty.
